title: Proper base change for Weil complexes
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$. Let $X'=X\times_YY'$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of $k_0$-schemes, with $k_0$-morphisms $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$. Assume that $f,f'$ are quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and that $Y,Y'$ are quasi-compact and locally of finite type over $k_0$. Suppose $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the native derived-Weil categories and actual operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]: on each geometric fibre $\bar T=T\times_{k_0}k$, the coefficient sheaf $B_{\bar T}$ consists of continuous $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-valued functions with locally finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-span; $\mathcal W_T$ is the abelian category of $B_{\bar T}$-modules with invertible geometric Frobenius structure; $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T)$ is the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal W_T)$ with bounded constructible cohomology. The functors $g^*,g'^*$ are induced termwise by the equivariant module inverse images, and $Rf_*,Rf'_*$ are the ordinary total right derived equivariant direct images, restricted to bounded constructible objects. Then for every $K\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$ there is an isomorphism of Weil complexes
$$g^*Rf_*K\ \cong\ Rf'_*g'^*K\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(Y').$$

proof.text: The field k₀ is Noetherian, so Spec k₀ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the structure maps of Y and Y′, whose local finite type hypotheses are already given [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Both bases are locally Noetherian and hence quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; in Lean QuasiSeparated.of_quasiSeparatedSpace supplies quasi-separatedness of their structure maps. Their quasi-compactness is already a hypothesis. No separatedness hypothesis is added.

proof.text: Equip the given IsPullback square with its canonical isomorphism to the chosen pullback: h.isoPullback, with projection equations h.isoPullback_hom_fst and h.isoPullback_hom_snd. Obtain the natural isomorphism with source the bounded constructible Weil subcategory of X and target the ambient native derived category of Y′; evaluate it at K.

proof.text: The functors WeilComplex.upperStar and WeilComplex.derivedLowerStar in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] are already restrictions of the actual ambient operations, with preservation proofs in their definitions. Thus both objects in the desired conclusion are already in the full subcategory. The component from step 2 has definitionally their underlying objects as endpoints. Apply ObjectProperty.isoMk to its forward and inverse maps; the inverse equations are inherited from the ambient category. This gives the required isomorphism in WeilComplex k₀ l Y′. No separate use of proper shriek-star coincidence or a new preservation theorem is needed.
